verdict.summary: Getting a working OAuth app on your own account is quick, and Composio's managed OAuth covers testing. Wider use is capped (25 unlisted marketplace installs, 10 allowlisted accounts for private apps), and public marketplace listing needs a manual HubSpot review that checks every requested scope.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 days (listing prep, scope trimming, and the listing form are the bulk; add time for domain verification and certification if you pursue them)
verdict.time_to_first_connection: 30-60 min with your own app (5 min with Composio managed OAuth)
verdict.approval_wait: None for own-account use and up to 25 unlisted installs. Listing: official initial review target is 10 business days (third-party reports say 2-4 weeks, unverified).

gates.unlocks: Create the app with the HubSpot CLI, set redirect URLs, and connect your own account through a test install.
limits: Test installs go to developer test accounts; you must tick the box to authorize an unverified app before Connect app.
Installing account must be a Super Admin or hold HubSpot Marketplace Access.
Until the Acceptable Use Policy is signed, installs stay limited to developer test accounts.

gates.name: Invited / unlisted installs (private or unlisted marketplace)
gates.unlocks: Install for invited customers: private OAuth app to allowlisted accounts, or unlisted marketplace app to up to 25 installs. Requires signing the AUP via Begin publishing.
limits: Private distributed OAuth apps: up to 10 allowlisted accounts (excluding developer test accounts).
Solutions Partners can raise the private OAuth allowlist to 100 accounts (not applicable to static-token apps).
Unlisted marketplace OAuth apps: 25 installs until listed.
Unlisted/unverified installs show an extra confirmation dialog for users.
Cap applies to apps created or migrated to Developer Platform 2025.2 (from 22 Sept 2025).
Installing users need Super Admin or HubSpot Marketplace Access.
gates.time_to_reach: Same day after AUP signature; allowlisting is handled by you in the app's distribution settings

gates.name: Marketplace listing (works for anyone) and optional Certification
gates.unlocks: Unlimited installs once listed, no unverified-app warning. Certification (separate, later) is needed for certified status.
limits: Listing requires OAuth as the only authorization method and at least three active unique production installs unaffiliated with your organization in the past 30 days.
Incomplete listing fields set the listing to Draft.
Rejected submissions must be fixed and resubmitted; full feedback loop is capped at 60 days.
Certification needs a verified domain, a security questionnaire, a demo video, 60 active unaffiliated installs, and six months of listing.
Certified status lasts two years, then must be renewed.
gates.time_to_reach: Official initial review target 10 business days after a complete submission; third-party reports 2-4 weeks (unverified). Only one app can be in review at a time.

steps.title: Decide your path: Composio managed OAuth first
steps.detail: For testing, use Composio's managed HubSpot OAuth app; it is available for the hubspot toolkit. Move to your own HubSpot app only when you need your own client ID/secret, your own redirect, or installs beyond the caps in Gate 2.
gotchas: Composio's default scope list is long. Do not ship it unchanged to a marketplace listing (see scope steps).

steps.title: Create a HubSpot developer account and install the CLI
steps.detail: Sign up for a HubSpot developer account (no paid plan or business verification was found in official pages; confirm in the console). Install the HubSpot CLI at v7.6.0 or later, which the docs require for new-platform apps.

steps.title: Create the project and app with the CLI
steps.detail: Run hs project create. When prompted, choose distribution (Marketplace, or restricted to specific accounts) and auth type OAuth (for multiple accounts). Choose restricted distribution if you only need private customer installs; you can change this later only by re-scoping the app.
gotchas: Pick distribution deliberately: it decides which install caps apply (Gate 2 limits differ between marketplace and private apps).

steps.title: Set the redirect URL
steps.detail: In app-hsmeta.json, add the Composio callback URL to the redirectUrls array in the auth block. The value must match exactly what Composio sends in the authorization request. Use https for anything beyond localhost testing; plain http is only allowed for localhost. Then run hs project upload.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Production redirect_uri must use https and a domain, not an IP address.
A mismatch between the registered redirect and the one in the authorization request causes the flow to fail.

steps.title: Declare scopes in the auth block, trimmed to what you use
steps.detail: Draft the requiredScopes, optionalScopes and conditionallyRequiredScopes lists in the auth block of app-hsmeta.json. Start from the scopes your code actually calls, not Composio's default list. Scopes marked as required fail the authorization page for any account without access, so put scope-by-account-tier items in optionalScopes or conditionallyRequiredScopes.
gotchas: Reviewers require every requested scope to be used; a past rejection asked for two scopes to be dropped after request logs showed only two APIs in use.
Sensitive CRM scopes need separate approval (see scope notes).

steps.title: Upload the project and copy client credentials
steps.detail: Run hs project upload. In the HubSpot developer console, go to Development > Projects, open your project, open the app by its UID, and go to the Auth tab. Copy the Client ID and Client secret under Client credentials. You can rotate the secret there.

values.label: Console path
values.value: Development > Projects > [project] > [app UID] > Auth > Client credentials

steps.title: Enter your credentials in Composio and run a test install
steps.detail: Enter the Client ID, Client secret and the Composio callback URL in your Composio auth config for HubSpot. Then, on the app's Distribution tab, use Test installs: tick the box to authorize the unverified app and click Connect app, using a developer test account.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Developer test accounts are excluded from the 25-install and 10-account limits per HubSpot's manage-apps page.

steps.title: Check token behavior before shipping
steps.detail: Run an authorization and confirm your code refreshes the access token. Access tokens expire after 30 minutes, so the refresh token must be used for long-running access. Store the refresh token securely and handle its rotation in code.
gotchas: Refresh token lifetime and expiry rules were not stated in the official pages consulted; test long-running access before relying on it.

steps.title: Sign the Acceptable Use Policy to leave developer test accounts
steps.detail: On the app's Distribution tab, click Begin publishing and review and sign the Acceptable Use Policy. Until this is signed, installs are limited to developer test accounts.

steps.title: Pick your Gate 2 distribution and invite customers
steps.detail: For a private app, add up to 10 allowlisted accounts (100 if you are a Solutions Partner and created the app in a Solutions Partner portal). For an unlisted marketplace app, you can reach up to 25 installs. Send customers the sample install URL from the Distribution tab. Installers must be Super Admin or have HubSpot Marketplace Access.
gotchas: Unlisted installs show a confirmation dialog to users; a listed app avoids it.
Whether the 25-install cap counts developer test accounts is not settled; official pages say test accounts are excluded.

steps.title: Verify your domain (certification prerequisite)
steps.detail: Add a verified domain to your developer account using the DNS TXT record shown in the console. Verification is usually within about an hour and can take up to 48 hours. Only one verified domain is allowed per developer account. Skip this if you only plan to list; a listed app does not need domain verification for the install prompt.
gotchas: A verified domain is required for certification, but a listed app does not need one for the install prompt.

steps.title: Prepare the listing fields and trim scopes
steps.detail: Draft the required listing fields: privacy policy and terms URLs (live), install button URL, setup documentation URL, support contact, a Shared data table that matches your scopes, and accurate pricing. Confirm every scope in the manifest is used by the app and remove the rest. Accept the Technology Partner Program Agreement.

values.label: Required listing fields
values.value: Privacy policy URL, terms URL, install button URL, setup docs URL, support contact, Shared data table, pricing

gotchas: Missing fields set the listing to Draft mode.
Three active unique production installs unaffiliated with your organization are required in the past 30 days first.

steps.title: Submit for listing review
steps.detail: Once you have at least three unaffiliated production installs and the listing fields are complete, submit the listing from the developer console. Only one app can be in review at a time. HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team reviews manually and rejects submissions that miss criteria.
gotchas: A rejected submission returns feedback; the full loop is capped at 60 days from when feedback is shared.

steps.title: Wait for review and respond to feedback
steps.detail: HubSpot's official target is an initial review within 10 business days. Third-party write-ups report 2 to 4 weeks, which is unverified. Respond to any feedback quickly to stay inside the 60-day window.

steps.title: Plan certification separately (optional, later)
steps.detail: Certification is a separate step from listing. It needs OAuth authorization-code flow with tokens refreshed without user involvement, a security questionnaire covering token handling, a demo video (required before HubSpot will review), 60 active unaffiliated installs, and six months of listing. Certified status lasts two years and must be renewed.
gotchas: HubSpot will not review without a demo video.
Whether the 10-business-day target and 60-day window apply to recertification or the 2026 security questionnaire is unconfirmed.

scopes.scope: Composio default scope list (about 35 scopes, e.g. crm.objects.contacts.write, settings.users.write, e-commerce)
scopes.effect: Requesting scopes you do not use will fail marketplace review. Trim to the scopes your code calls before listing. Tier for most individual scopes was not verified in the findings.

scopes.scope: Sensitive and highly sensitive CRM data scopes (e.g. *.sensitive.read, *.highly_sensitive.read)
scopes.effect: Not self-service for marketplace-bound apps. You must request access from the Ecosystem Quality team, which allowlists them for testing before publication. The installing account needs an Enterprise subscription.

scopes.scope: Required vs optional scopes (requiredScopes, optionalScopes, conditionallyRequiredScopes)
scopes.effect: Checked scopes are treated as required: a missing scope errors the authorization page, and accounts without access cannot install. Put tier-dependent scopes in optional or conditionally required lists so the install still works.

blockers.symptom: Listing submission rejected for requesting scopes the app does not use.
blockers.cause: Reviewers require every requested scope to be used; Composio's default scope list is long.
blockers.fix: Trim requiredScopes, optionalScopes and conditionallyRequiredScopes to the scopes your code calls, re-upload with hs project upload, and resubmit.

blockers.symptom: Listing stays in Draft mode after submission.
blockers.cause: One or more required listing fields is missing or not live (privacy policy, terms, install URL, setup docs, support contact, Shared data table, pricing).
blockers.fix: Complete every field and confirm each URL loads publicly, then resubmit.

blockers.symptom: Install hits the 25-install limit or a 10-account limit on a private app.
blockers.cause: Unlisted marketplace apps are capped at 25 installs; private OAuth apps at 10 allowlisted accounts (100 for Solutions Partners).
blockers.fix: List the app on the Marketplace to remove the marketplace cap, or switch to a private app with a larger allowlist if you qualify as a Solutions Partner.

blockers.symptom: A sensitive CRM scope cannot be requested or the install fails for a customer.
blockers.cause: Sensitive scopes need Ecosystem Quality allowlisting, and the installing account needs an Enterprise subscription.
blockers.fix: Request the scope from the Ecosystem Quality team before publication, and declare it as conditionally required or optional so non-Enterprise accounts can still install.

blockers.symptom: Your app is a legacy public app created before 23 June 2026.
blockers.cause: Legacy public apps run on the pre-Projects architecture. HubSpot announced they become unsupported from 15 September 2026 (already passed as of today, 2026-10-28), with enforcement in September 2027, and says they must migrate to stay listed.
blockers.fix: Migrate the app to the Projects-based model before listing or certification. Check your app's creation date and architecture in the console.

blockers.symptom: Cannot create a new legacy private app.
blockers.cause: Reported (unverified, from a third-party GitHub PR) that legacy private app creation was disabled 26 Oct 2026 for existing accounts and 28 Sept 2026 for new ones, with service keys as the replacement.
blockers.fix: Do not rely on legacy private apps for new work. Build on the Projects-based app model; confirm the cutoff and the service-key replacement directly with HubSpot before planning around it.

blockers.symptom: Listing review takes longer than expected.
blockers.cause: Official initial review target is 10 business days, but third-party write-ups report 2 to 4 weeks. Only one app can be in review at a time.
blockers.fix: Plan around 2-4 weeks as a conservative estimate. Keep feedback turnaround fast; the full loop is capped at 60 days from when feedback is shared.

composio.note: Use Composio managed OAuth for quick testing. You need your own HubSpot app (own client ID/secret and own redirect) when you need to go beyond the install caps: unlisted marketplace OAuth apps stop at 25 installs, private OAuth apps at 10 allowlisted accounts (100 for Solutions Partners). Listing removes the marketplace cap. Composio's default scope list is long and includes scopes most apps will not need. HubSpot reviewers check that every requested scope is used, so trim before any listing submission.

evidence.claim: Composio already offers managed OAuth for HubSpot, with the HubSpot authorize and token URLs and a default scope list.
evidence.quote: managed_oauth_available": true

evidence.claim: Certification (a separate step from listing) needs a verified domain, OAuth authorization-code flow with tokens refreshed without user involvement, a security questionnaire covering token handling, a demo video (HubSpot will not review without one), and at least 60 active unaffiliated unique installs; the app must also have been listed for six months.
evidence.quote: HubSpot will not review your app unless you submit a demo video as instructed

evidence.claim: Certified status lasts two years and then needs renewal; if an app falls out of compliance, HubSpot can start recertification early or unpublish it.
evidence.quote: App certifications are valid on a rolling basis for two years, and must be renewed.

evidence.claim: Reviewers require every requested scope to be used: extra scopes must be removed, and scopes that only some customers need should be declared as conditionally required or optional. A reviewer's example rejection cited 30 days of request logs showing only two APIs in use and asked for two scopes to be dropped.
evidence.quote: Use all scopes it requests for installation

evidence.claim: Sensitive and highly sensitive CRM data scopes are not self-service for marketplace-bound apps: you request them from the Ecosystem Quality team, which allowlists them for testing before publication, and the installing account needs an Enterprise subscription.
evidence.quote: you'll need to request access to specific sensitive scopes from HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team

evidence.claim: Checked scopes in the Auth settings are treated as required: if they are missing from the authorization request, the authorization page errors, and a user whose account lacks access to a scope cannot install the app. Optional scopes are dropped automatically for accounts without access.
evidence.quote: Any scopes that you've checked off in your app's Auth settings will be treated as required

evidence.claim: The app is created with the HubSpot CLI (hs project create), where you choose distribution (marketplace or restricted to specific accounts) and auth type (OAuth for multiple accounts or a static token for one account).
evidence.quote: select whether you plan to distribute your app on the HubSpot Marketplace or if want to restrict installation to specific HubSpot accounts.

evidence.claim: Scopes are declared in the auth block of app-hsmeta.json as requiredScopes, optionalScopes and conditionallyRequiredScopes, then pushed with hs project upload; the Auth tab then shows them under Scopes.
evidence.quote: edit the corresponding scopes within the `auth` property of your app's `app-hsmeta.json`

evidence.claim: Redirect URLs are set in the redirectUrls array of the auth block in app-hsmeta.json (localhost http is shown for development), then uploaded with hs project upload. The redirect must be registered exactly as used in the authorization request.
evidence.quote: Add one or more valid redirect URLs to the app-hsmeta.json file

evidence.claim: Production redirect_uri must use https (http is allowed only for localhost testing), must use a domain rather than an IP address, and must match what is configured on the app's Auth settings.
evidence.quote: For security reasons, this URL must use `https` in production.

evidence.claim: Client ID and client secret are on the app's Auth tab under Client credentials (reached via Development > Projects > project > app UID); the secret can be rotated there.
evidence.quote: Under *Client credentials*, copy the *Client ID* and *Client secret* from your new app

evidence.claim: Unlisted HubSpot marketplace OAuth apps are capped at 25 installs until the Ecosystem Quality team reviews and lists them; after listing, installs are unlimited.
evidence.quote: Until your app is reviewed by the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team and listed on the Marketplace, you'll be limited to 25 installs.

evidence.claim: Installs of a new app start with a developer test account (Test installs on the Distribution tab), where you tick a box to authorize an unverified app before connecting; a standard-account install needs Super Admin or HubSpot Marketplace Access permissions.
evidence.quote: select the **checkbox** to authorize installing an unverified app, then click **Connect app**.

evidence.claim: Installing users must be a Super Admin or hold HubSpot Marketplace Access permission; for OAuth marketplace apps, install from the sample install URL in the Distribution tab.
evidence.quote: must either be a [Super Admin] or have [HubSpot Marketplace Access] permissions.

evidence.claim: To distribute beyond developer test accounts you must sign HubSpot's Acceptable Use Policy via Begin publishing on the Distribution tab; until it is signed, installs are limited to developer test accounts.
evidence.quote: Review and sign the Acceptable Use Policy (AUP).

evidence.claim: A verified domain (one per developer account, set up through a DNS TXT record and usually verified within about an hour, up to 48 hours) is a certification requirement; verifying it changes the install prompt to show the domain, but a banner still says the app has not been reviewed until it is listed.
evidence.quote: You can only have one verified domain per developer account.

evidence.claim: Access tokens expire after 30 minutes, and the refresh token is the long-term credential used to get a new access token; the authorization code is single-use and must be exchanged within a short window.
evidence.quote: expires after 30 minutes.

evidence.claim: Legacy public apps created before 23 June 2026 are on the pre-Projects architecture; HubSpot announced them unsupported from 15 September 2026, with enforcement in September 2027, and says they must migrate to the Projects model to stay listed.
evidence.quote: To remain listed in the Marketplace and retain certification, migrate to the current Projects-based app model.

evidence.claim: Legacy private app creation is reportedly disabled from 26 October 2026 for existing accounts (28 September for new accounts), with service keys as the replacement; this comes from a third-party GitHub PR, not HubSpot, so verify before relying on it.
evidence.quote: Legacy private app creation disabled 2026-10-26 (existing accounts), 2026-09-28 (new)

evidence.claim: Third-party write-ups report a typical 2 to 4 week wait for listing review, but these are non-official and vary; the official target is 10 business days for the initial review.
evidence.quote: Timeline in 2026: 2-4 weeks for most submissions

evidence.claim: The developer-portal create-app documentation page loads without a login wall (HTTP 200), and new-platform apps are initialized with the HubSpot CLI, which requires CLI v7.6.0 or later per the docs.
evidence.quote: Apps on the new developer platform (versions `2025.2` and `2026.03`) are initialized using the HubSpot CLI

evidence.claim: Privately distributed OAuth apps can be installed in up to 10 allowlisted accounts (excluding developer test accounts); static token apps are limited to one standard account plus up to 10 developer test accounts.
evidence.quote: Privately distributed OAuth apps: can be installed in up to 10 allowlisted accounts

evidence.claim: Listed apps that are certified show no unverified-app warning and do not need domain verification for the install prompt, because HubSpot's review covers them.
evidence.quote: You are not required to verify the domain if your app has been listed on the HubSpot Marketplace

evidence.claim: Solutions Partners can raise the private OAuth allowlist to 100 accounts; that override does not apply to static-token private apps.
evidence.quote: up to 100 customer portals when the app is created in a Solutions Partner portal

evidence.claim: The 25-install cap took effect on 22 September 2025 for apps created or migrated to Developer Platform version 2025.2, and migrated legacy public apps already above 25 installs have the cap enforced automatically.
evidence.quote: apps that are created or migrated to version 2025.2 are capped at 25 installs until they are listed on the HubSpot Marketplace.

evidence.claim: Since 23 March 2026, users who install an unlisted or unverified marketplace app see an extra confirmation dialog, and listed apps are unaffected; HubSpot suggests listing to give users a smoother install.
evidence.quote: Show a confirmation dialog before completing the installation.

evidence.claim: Listing minimums: OAuth must be the only authorization method, the listed app needs at least three active unique production installs unaffiliated with your organization over the past 30 days, you must only request needed scopes, and you must accept the Technology Partner Program Agreement.
evidence.quote: Installs: your app must have at least three active, unique installs.

evidence.claim: Listing submissions are reviewed manually by the Ecosystem Quality team and are rejected if they miss the criteria. The initial review target is 10 business days and the full feedback loop is capped at 60 days from when feedback is shared. Only one app can be in review at a time.
evidence.quote: the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team will complete an initial review within 10 business days.

evidence.claim: Listing also needs complete listing fields: live privacy policy and terms URLs, a live install button URL, a setup documentation URL, a support contact, a Shared data table that matches the scopes, and accurate pricing. Missing fields set the listing to Draft.
evidence.quote: failure to meet these requirements will cause your listing to be set to Draft mode only

open_questions: Whether a Technology Partner Program membership is required to list. The listing page requires accepting the agreement; third-party blogs say no membership is needed, which is not verified officially.
Developer account prerequisites beyond a free HubSpot developer account (paid plan, org admin, or business verification) were not found in fetched official pages.
The full official scope catalog and which scopes are restricted. Only the sensitive and highly sensitive CRM scopes were confirmed.
Refresh token lifetime and expiry rules were not stated in the official pages consulted.
Whether the 25-install cap counts developer test accounts. Official manage-apps page says test accounts are excluded from the 25 and 10 limits, but this was not confirmed in full.
Whether unlisted marketplace installs (up to 25) need any HubSpot review before the first install. The findings imply they do not, but no page states it directly.
Whether the 10-business-day initial review and 60-day feedback window apply unchanged to recertification or to the 2026 security questionnaire.
Whether the legacy private app creation cutoff (26 Oct 2026) is accurate. Sourced only to a third-party GitHub PR, not a HubSpot changelog.
How HubSpot rejects an unknown client_id at the authorize endpoint remains unconfirmed; the probe returned a generic 200 page.
How the Composio auth config is filled in for a custom HubSpot app (exact field labels) was not covered by the findings; check Composio's UI.
